ov: The European polecat: a dark brown mustelid with a pale belly and a dark mask across its face. It is famous for a foul-smelling liquid it uses to mark its territory, and is thought to be the sole wild ancestor of the ferret, domesticated over 2,000 years ago.
rg: Europe and the Rif mountains of Morocco.
df: Small rodents, birds, amphibians and reptiles.
fx: It sometimes paralyses prey with a bite to the brain and stores it, still alive, in its burrow.
Its Latin name putorius means "stench", the root of the English word putrid.
